Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
UniFi OS unauthenticated RCE chain exploit attempt via nginx URI-normalization bypass (CVE-2026-34908/9/10) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to UniFi OS Server (default TCP 11443) that abuse the auth-exempt prefix /api/auth/validate-sso/ combined with percent-encoded path traversal to reach the protected ucs/update/latest_package command-injection handler. This is the exact Bishop Fox-documented bypass where the auth module reads the raw URI while nginx routes on the normalized URI. Rationale: Built on the Bishop Fox-confirmed exact signature: auth-exempt prefix '/api/auth/validate-sso/' + encoded traversal ('..%2f','..%2e','%2e%2e') routing to the 'ucs/update/latest_package' handler on TCP 11443. The prefix+traversal combination is the unique fingerprint of the raw-vs-normalized URI bypass and is not produced by legitimate clients. Cross-checked against: • https://bishopfox.com/blog/popping-root-on-unifi-os-server-unauthenticated-rce-chain-detection-analysis • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-unifi-os-bug-lets-hackers-gain-root-without-authentication/ • https://www.securityweek.com/critical-ubiquiti-vulnerabilities-in-attackers-crosshairs/ • https://github.com/BishopFox/CVE-2026-34908-check
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bishop Fox CVE-2026-34908-check safe-detection script run by your own vuln team
  • Authenticated vulnerability scanners (Tenable/Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the path
  • Authorized red-team / pentest engagement against the UniFi controller
  • Security researchers internet-wide scanning (will show external SourceIP, no follow-on)
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has "BishopFox" and RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Nmap","masscan","Rapid7")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the SourceIP and whether it is internal/external; check the DeviceAction (allowed vs blocked) and HTTP status — a 200 to the validate-sso+traversal request indicates a vulnerable, reachable target. Correlate the timestamp with UC2 (post-exploit shell) on the controller host. 2) Contain: block the SourceIP at the perimeter and restrict TCP 11443 to management VLAN/VPN only; if a 200 was returned, isolate the UniFi OS Server pending forensic review. 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host for new processes under the ucs-update service account, outbound reverse-shell connections, and confirm firmware is patched (UniFi OS Server >= fixed SAB-064 build).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/auth/validate-sso/"
| where RequestURL has_any ("..%2f", "..%2e", "%2e%2e", "latest_package")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

UniFi OS Server post-exploit reverse shell from ucs-update / unifi service account (CVE-2026-34910) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts a self-hosted UniFi OS Server (Windows/Linux, EDR-onboarded) where the UniFi backend or the ucs-update service account spawns a command interpreter or netcat with reverse-shell indicators. This is the execution stage of the CVE-2026-34910 command injection that lands in the package-name parameter and runs as root. Rationale: Grounds on Bishop Fox's stated post-exploit indicator ('unexpected child processes under the ucs-update service account') plus the fact that the CVE-2026-34910 injection executes as root via the package handler. The differentiator from benign package updates is the reverse-shell command-line tokens (/dev/tcp, mkfifo, nc -e, socket.socket), which the legitimate ucs-update workflow never emits. Cross-checked against: • https://bishopfox.com/blog/popping-root-on-unifi-os-server-unauthenticated-rce-chain-detection-analysis • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-unifi-os-bug-lets-hackers-gain-root-without-authentication/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ucs-update package operations invoking sh -c to run apt/dpkg (no reverse-shell tokens, filtered out)
  • Admin troubleshooting on the controller via interactive bash session
  • Backup/monitoring scripts using curl/nc for health checks
  • Custom UniFi automation that legitimately shells out (rare)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("apt-get","dpkg","apt ","yum ","dnf ") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("/dev/tcp/","nc -e","mkfifo"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree on the affected host (parent chain back to the UniFi/nginx service) and capture the reverse-shell command line and any destination IP/port. Cross-reference the timestamp with UC1 inbound exploit hits on TCP 11443. 2) Contain: kill the spawned process, isolate the UniFi OS Server host from the network, and block the C2 destination at the egress firewall. 3) Hunt: search for persistence (new cron entries, modified UniFi startup scripts, new SSH keys), additional ucs-update-spawned children across all controllers, and credential/config theft from the UniFi datastore.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("ucs-update","unifi") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("unifi-core","UniFi OS Server","/usr/lib/unifi")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","netcat","python","python3","perl","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","mkfifo","bash -i","sh -i","socket.socket","nc -e","ncat -e","-e /bin","Net.Sockets","Invoke-")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername has_any ("ucs-update","unifi") or ParentProcessName has_any ("unifi","ucs","unifi-core")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","netcat","python","python3","perl","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","mkfifo","bash -i","sh -i","socket.socket","nc -e","ncat -e","-e /bin","Net.Sockets")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: UniFi OS Server Service Account Spawns Reverse Shell (CVE-2026-34910)
id: b41d8a77-2e6c-4d09-9a1f-6f3c2e5b7d40
description: Detects the UniFi backend or the ucs-update service account spawning a shell, scripting interpreter, or netcat with reverse-shell command-line indicators, consistent with post-exploitation of the UniFi OS command-injection chain.
references:
  - https://bishopfox.com/blog/popping-root-on-unifi-os-server-unauthenticated-rce-chain-detection-analysis
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/25
tags:

logsource:

detection:

level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@user.name:ucs-update OR @user.name:unifi*) (@process.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR nc OR ncat OR netcat OR python OR python3 OR perl)) @process.command_line:(*"/dev/tcp/"* OR *mkfifo* OR *"bash -i"* OR *"nc -e"* OR *"-e /bin"* OR *socket.socket*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|nc|ncat|netcat|python3?|perl)$/i

| regex("(/dev/tcp/|mkfifo|bash -i|socket\.socket|nc -e|-e /bin/)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

KEV exposure hunt: UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 actively-exploited CVEs present in fleet AIReconnaissance Medium
Surfaces managed assets (notably self-hosted UniFi OS Server hosts) whose vulnerability inventory still reports the four CISA-KEV CVEs from this advisory, prioritising internet-facing devices. Covers the Lantronix EDS5000 command-injection flaw (CVE-2025-67038) which has no published request signature, plus the UniFi OS chain. Rationale: Uses the exact CISA-KEV CVE identifiers from the article (CVE-2026-34908/9/10 for UniFi OS, CVE-2025-67038 for Lantronix EDS5000). Joining to DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing prioritises the externally reachable assets that match the unauthenticated/remote exploitation profile and the June 26 2026 FCEB remediation deadline. Caveat: TVM only covers assets onboarded to Defender (e.g. self-hosted UniFi OS Server); standalone Lantronix/UniFi appliances will need a dedicated network scan. Cross-checked against: • https://securityaffairs.com/194142/security/u-s-cisa-adds-ubiquiti-unifi-os-and-lantronix-eds5000-plugin-flaws-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-069-02 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-warns-of-max-severity-ubiquiti-flaws-exploited-in-attacks/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Devices already patched but TVM inventory cache is stale (re-scan to confirm)
  • Decommissioned/retired assets still present in the inventory
  • Duplicate device records inflating the count
  • Internal-only devices flagged as exposed but actually behind segmentation (lower priority, not a true FP)
Response runbook
1) Triage: rank results by IsInternetFacing then severity; confirm running firmware/build against the fixed versions (UniFi OS Server SAB-064 fixed build; Lantronix EDS5000 2.2.0.0R1). 2) Contain: for any internet-facing match, restrict UniFi management to TCP 11443 on a trusted segment/VPN and place ACLs on the Lantronix web RPC interface until patched; meet the CISA FCEB June 26 2026 deadline. 3) Hunt: for each exposed device, run UC1 (inbound exploit signature) and UC2 (post-exploit shell) over the lookback window to determine whether exposure has already been exploited.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-34908","CVE-2026-34909","CVE-2026-34910","CVE-2025-67038")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, CveId asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, CveId asc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
